audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls the ability "Powder Kegs" in seven places (tldr, phases[1].why, phases[3].why, phases[5].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].t, dosFull[2].d). The ability is Powder Keg, singular.
audit.why: Riot's name is Powder Keg. The suspectNames scan flagged only the Let's Bounce false positive and missed this one entirely, so it survived into every string that discusses the matchup's supposed core cooldown.
audit.corrected: Replaced throughout, and re-pointed those strings at Remove Scurvy, which is the cooldown that actually matters.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry is built on "track Powder Keg" and "only engage once it is down". Powder Keg has no cooldown in the normal sense — the kit lists it as 0, because it is a stock/charge ability.
audit.why: Telling a player to engage when Powder Keg is down describes a window that never opens: Gangplank holds keg charges more or less permanently. This is worse than the analogous Galio problem, where at least the tracked cooldown existed. The genuine punish window is Remove Scurvy at 22/20/18/16/14s, which also carries a 60-100 mana cost, so a Gangplank who spends it is both CC-vulnerable and mana-poor.
audit.corrected: Re-pointed the tracked cooldown to Remove Scurvy at 22s and stated that kegs are denied by positioning, not by waiting.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two strings claim Gangplank heals off Parrrley: spikes[1].text ("he can Q-heal off your minions") and wants.foe[1] ("Q-heal and kite with barrel slows").
audit.why: Parrrley does not heal. Riot's text is "Shoots target, plundering Gold for each enemy unit killed" — it is a gold and poke tool. Gangplank's only healing is Remove Scurvy. This matters because it changes which cooldown the player respects: a Zac who believes Gangplank sustains off every Q will disengage poke wars he should be winning.
audit.corrected: Removed the invented Q healing from both strings.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gangplank.json (Parrrley; heal flag appears only on Remove Scurvy)

audit.whatIsWrong: The content chart gave Gangplank 6 of 7 stages while Zac wins 52.33% over 258 games, and the full layer disagreed with it on four stages (full read GP/Skill/Zac/Zac/GP/Zac/Zac).
audit.why: Neither chart described the matchup shape correctly. Zac genuinely owns levels 3-5 — his full kit is online, Gangplank has no dash and his only escape is barrel movement speed plus a Remove Scurvy cleanse. Gangplank genuinely owns the item stages as a scaling crit carry. The content chart erased the Zac window; the full chart erased the Gangplank scaling.
audit.corrected: Set both layers to Gangplank/Skill/Zac/Zac/Skill/Gangplank/Gangplank — Zac owns his 3-5 window, Gangplank outscales, level 6 is genuinely split.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why for Level 6 was the same boilerplate seen across this champion's file — "Elastic Slingshot from fog + R bounces win every river fight" — while the side label said Gangplank.
audit.why: Cannon Barrage is global with a slow zone, so its lane role is disengage rather than kill pressure, while Zac's own ultimate is a hard engage onto a squishy target. The stage is contested, and the boilerplate said nothing about either ultimate.
audit.corrected: Rewrote to describe both ultimates and set the stage to Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] pairs the title "Let him free-scale" with the body "Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown", and dosFull[2] pairs "E-knock him up" with a body about wasted cooldowns.
audit.why: The same generator template mismatch found in the Darius, Fiora and Galio entries. It appears in every Zac matchup I audited, so it is systemic rather than per-matchup.
audit.corrected: Re-pointed the mismatched title and body.

notes: Three separate defect classes in this one matchup. (1) "Powder Kegs" appears seven times in the full layer; the ability is Powder Keg. The suspectNames scan missed it while flagging the Let's Bounce false positive, which suggests the scan is tuned too tight. (2) The entry's entire spine was "engage when Powder Keg is down" — but Powder Keg is a stock ability with cooldown 0 in the kit, so that window never opens. This is the most misleading thing I found in the slice: it reads like concrete cooldown advice and is unactionable. I re-pointed it at Remove Scurvy (22s at rank 1, 60-100 mana). (3) Parrrley was described as healing him in two places; it plunders gold and does not heal, and Remove Scurvy is his only sustain. That is the same fabricated-heal pattern I found on Galio's Winds of War in this slice — two different champions, two invented heals, so it is worth a systematic pass for heal claims that no kit flag supports. NOT ASSERTED: whether Remove Scurvy can cleanse Zac's Q pull or E knockup. Displacement is usually not cleansable, but cleanse eligibility is explicitly one of the things the kit files mark unknown, so the text says only that Scurvy cures crowd control without claiming it beats a specific Zac ability. The existing spikes[2] line "Remove Scurvy cleanses your CC" carries that same unverified implication and I left it rather than extend it.
